title: Geometric inverse image commutes with derived singleton extension
statement:
Let $u:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $B_{Y,1}\leftarrow B_{Y,2}\leftarrow\cdots$ be sheaves of commutative rings and set $B_{X,j}=u^{-1}B_{Y,j}$, including the pulled-back transitions. A strict system is a sequence of $B_{T,j}$-module sheaves with $B_{T,j+1}$-linear maps to the scalar restriction of level $j$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of these systems and of level modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $G_B$ for exact termwise inverse image, $u_n^*$ for inverse image on $B_{Y,n}$-modules, $e_n^T$ for derived evaluation, and $L_n^T\dashv e_n^T$ for the total left derived ordinary singleton extension [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], [lem-pur-system-single-derived-extension]. Its ordinary value at $j\le n$ is $B_{T,j}\otimes_{B_{T,n}}Q$, and is zero at $j>n$.

There is a natural isomorphism of functors to the derived category of strict $B_X$-systems
$$c_n:G_BL_n^Y\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n^Xu_n^*.$$
For a flat-term K-flat $B_{Y,n}$-complex $Q$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], the ordinary singleton complex is K-flat with flat terms on the ringed sequence site. Both sides of $c_n$ are computed on that same $Q$. Its representative at $j\le n$ is the canonical tensor/pullback map
$$u_j^*(B_{Y,j}\otimes_{B_{Y,n}}Q)\longrightarrow B_{X,j}\otimes_{B_{X,n}}u_n^*Q,$$
and at $j>n$ it is the identity of zero. These representatives commute with the actual system transitions. At $j=n$, multiplication identifies $e_n^Xc_n$ with the identity of $u_n^*$. The isomorphisms also intertwine the canonical maps $L_n^T(B_{T,n}\otimes^L_{B_{T,m}}(-))\to L_m^T$ for $m\ge n$ (the singleton maps whose below-$n$ components are the tensor associators and whose other components are zero), using the canonical scalar/pullback comparisons. No boundedness or coefficient-flatness hypothesis is imposed.
